subject: Media Literacy
title: Lateral Reading
description: A quick, practical guide to Lateral Reading.

hook.text: Fact-checkers spend less time on a website than students — because they immediately open new tabs to verify.

buildup.text: Lateral reading means leaving a source's website to check what others say about it, instead of evaluating it in isolation.

discovery.text: Stanford researchers found that professional fact-checkers use lateral reading while students read vertically.

twist.text: A polished website can fool vertical readers. Lateral readers quickly find if the source is legitimate.

climax.text: The fastest way to evaluate a source isn't reading more of it — it's checking what others say about it.

quiz.question: What is lateral reading?
options: Reading more content on the same website
Leaving the site to check what others say about the source
Reading news in a foreign language
